title: An End-to-End Coding Scheme for DNA-Based Data Storage With Nanopore Sequenced Reads
author: Sokolovskii, Roman
license_note: Zenodo record metadata license field: cc-by-4.0

steps.title: Obtain synthesized oligo pool
steps.instruction: Order a pool of 91,766 oligonucleotides, each 150 nucleotides long, from GenScript (file oligos.fasta). Each oligo contains a 110‑nt pseudo‑random payload flanked by 20‑nt primers on both ends.

steps.title: Divide pool into three groups
steps.instruction: Split the synthesized pool into three roughly equal groups: two groups of 30,589 oligos and one group of 30,588 oligos.

steps.title: Assign primer pairs to groups
steps.instruction: For each of the three groups, use the dedicated primer pair listed in primers_synthesis.fasta for targeted PCR amplification.

steps.title: PCR‑amplify each group
steps.instruction: For each file (0, 1, 2), take a sample from the corresponding group and perform PCR amplification using its specific primer pair.

steps.title: Prepare amplicon library for MinION
steps.instruction: Prepare the PCR products for sequencing on an Oxford Nanopore Technologies MinION device following the standard ONT library‑preparation protocol for amplicon DNA.

steps.title: Basecall raw MinION reads
steps.instruction: Run Guppy basecalling on the raw MinION reads in two modes: fast (parameter acc‑false) and high‑accuracy (parameter acc‑true).

substeps.instruction: Fast mode: use Guppy with acc‑false.
High‑accuracy mode: use Guppy with acc‑true.

steps.title: Separate reads by quality score
steps.instruction: For each basecalling mode, split the reads into two groups based on the quality‑score threshold of 8: reads that pass (label "passQ‑true") and reads that fail (label "passQ‑false").

steps.title: Identify primer‑containing segments
steps.instruction: Perform a BLAST‑based fuzzy search for the forward and reverse‑complement primer sequences on each read group. Retain only alignments where the primers are located at a distance of 150 ± 15 nucleotides.

steps.title: Extract and separate segments
steps.instruction: From the qualifying alignments, extract the DNA segments between the primer pairs, creating separate collections for forward‑read segments and reverse‑complement (backward) read segments.

steps.title: Assign segments to original strands
steps.instruction: For each extracted segment, compute the Levenshtein distance to every synthesized strand and assign the segment to the closest original strand.

steps.title: Archive clustered read segments
steps.instruction: Package the resulting clusters into the archive clustered_read_segments.tar.gz, which contains 12 sub‑archives (one for each combination of file 0/1/2, accuracy acc‑true/acc‑false, and Q‑score passQ‑true/passQ‑false). Within each sub‑archive, include two folders (forward and backward) each containing a TX file (reference synthesized sequences) and an RX file (received segment clusters). Use a line of "===============================" as a separator between entries in the RX files.
